title: skills sync reports a conflict for skills whose canon and installed trees are byte-identical
body:
**`intent claude skills sync` reports `changed upstream AND here -- HELD` for three skills whose canon and installed trees are BYTE-IDENTICAL, and the message it prints tells the operator that forcing will discard their work.** There is provably nothing to discard. Measured 2026-09-08.

**THE THREE CHECKSUMS, COMPUTED WITH `payload.rs`'s OWN ALGORITHM** (relative path + NUL + sha256(content) + LF, over the whole tree, `checksum_scope: tree` as the live manifest declares):

| skill | canon | installed | manifest | canon==installed | verdict printed |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `in-tca-audit` | `262b9722` | `262b9722` | `5bc75387` | **TRUE** | HELD |
| `in-tca-finish` | `5254cb07` | `5254cb07` | `2cc0689f` | **TRUE** | HELD |
| `in-tca-init` | `d480f44f` | `d480f44f` | `fc70bb78` | **TRUE** | HELD |
| `in-standards` | `220f7d20` | `eb042d76` | `eb042d76` | false | `updated` -- CORRECT |
| `in-detrope` | `60a1dc29` | `60a1dc29` | `60a1dc29` | true | `up to date` -- CORRECT |

**THE MECHANISM.** The conflict test is evidently `canon != manifest` (upstream changed) AND `installed != manifest` (changed here). Both limbs are true for the three above -- but only because the MANIFEST is stale, recorded `2026-04-28`. **When canon and installed agree, there is no conflict to resolve whatever the baseline says; both sides are the same bytes.** The honest verdict is *up to date, baseline refreshed*, not *needs a decision*. The two correct rows above show the logic works whenever the manifest is current, so this is a missing case rather than a broken comparison.

**`in-essentials` IS THE FOURTH HELD ROW AND ITS `changed here` LIMB IS ALSO FALSE.** Its installed tree is byte-identical to canon at `HEAD~1` -- diffed, empty -- so it carries no local edit; it matches a PRIOR canon while the manifest (recorded `2026-08-25`) records neither. Same root: **the manifest is not a reliable record of what is installed, and the whole conflict verdict rests on it.**

**WHY THIS IS WORSE THAN A COSMETIC WRONG VERDICT.** The message reads *`--force` takes the source copy and reports the checksum of what it discarded; copy your edits out first if you want them*. An operator who believes it will decline to force, correctly, on the evidence in front of them -- and the skill then stays stale permanently. **The safe reading and the correct action point in opposite directions.**

**AND IT LANDS ON THE ONE PATH THAT MATTERS FOR `ST0056 AC-15.3`**, which requires that a change carried out through `intent claude skills` REACHES a consumer, asserted by driving a consumer install. A correction landed in canon today (`20841a5e8`, striking a frontmatter format v3 has never written, in `in-essentials` -- the skill `/in-session` loads every session) cannot reach any consumer on this machine except by overriding a warning that falsely implies data loss. **4 of 23 skills are in this state.**

**NOT CLAIMED, and it is the next measurement rather than a gap in this one:** why the baselines went stale. A failed manifest write, a sync that copied without recording, or an install path that never writes one are all consistent with what is here, and distinguishing them needs the write path read rather than the compare path.

Reported by vc; routed to cc, who owns `payload.rs`'s neighbourhood and was idle. Corroborates from a third angle that skills are tree-scoped in v3: the live manifest's own `checksum_scope` field reads `tree`.
